861: A is correct because Provisioned IOPS SSD storage on an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance dedicates a fixed number of input/output operations per second to the database, which directly addresses the performance impact of the high volume of write operations. Amazon CloudWatch provides the write-ops and IOPS metrics needed to observe database performance, and provisioned IOPS can be adjusted as workload demands change. General Purpose SSD or an ElastiCache caching layer would not solve a write-heavy bottleneck because caching primarily accelerates reads, and EFS or DocumentDB are not the right managed MySQL migration targets.
862: D is correct because client-side encryption with a key stored in AWS KMS encrypts the archival files within the application before they ever leave the company's environment, guaranteeing that no third party can access plaintext data in transit to AWS. When the encrypted objects are stored in the existing S3 bucket, only the KMS key holder can decrypt them, giving the company full control over the encryption process. Server-side encryption options like SSE-KMS would only encrypt the data after it arrives at AWS, which fails the requirement that data be protected before it is sent.
863: B is correct because RDS automated backups natively support a configurable retention period, so simply setting the retention to 30 days produces a daily automated backup with no additional tooling or scripting. This is a managed feature that requires only a one-time configuration change and therefore has the least operational overhead. The other options all require building or manually running custom snapshot processes, such as Lambda functions, CLI commands, or Systems Manager schedules, which add unnecessary administration.
864: C is correct because an Aurora read replica can be added to the existing DB cluster with a single action and shares the same underlying storage as the writer instance, making it far cheaper than provisioning an entire second Aurora cluster or a Redshift cluster. Directing read-only queries to the reader endpoint and write queries to the cluster (writer) endpoint offloads the read workload from the writer instance, improving write performance during peak usage. Aurora also replicates to the replica with millisecond lag, so users see current data without any custom copy jobs.
865: A is correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, serverless ingestion service that can reliably capture the large, near-real-time stream of incoming data and scale automatically with the traffic, eliminating the latency caused by overwhelmed ingestion. E is correct because AWS Fargate with Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for containers that can run the 30-minute processing job at scale, automatically launching and removing containers as data volumes fluctuate. Lambda with Step Functions would be constrained by the 15-minute function timeout, and EC2 Auto Scaling groups or AWS DMS are not serverless and are not designed for this streaming ingestion and processing pattern.
866: A is correct because a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 provides a private connection between the VPC and S3 that routes traffic over the AWS private network without ever traversing the public internet. Adding the endpoint route to the VPC route table ensures the EC2 instances' traffic to the bucket stays private, satisfying the requirement that sensitive data never be sent over the public internet. An NLB cannot target an S3 bucket, S3 buckets cannot be deployed inside a VPC, and Direct Connect is a costly physical connection that does not attach to S3 regional endpoints.
867: D is correct because AWS Compute Optimizer is the purpose-built service that analyzes configuration and utilization metrics of EC2 instances and EBS volumes and generates right-sizing recommendations, including projected monthly cost savings for each recommendation. Its findings directly satisfy both the analysis and the estimated savings opportunity requirements with no custom work. Inspector, Systems Manager, and CloudWatch do not produce EBS volume cost-optimization recommendations with estimated savings.
868: B is correct because Amazon S3 Storage Lens delivers organization-wide object storage analytics across all Regions and accounts, and its bucket-level dashboard explicitly reports versioning status so administrators can identify every bucket that is not versioning-enabled. It can aggregate views across the entire organization, which matches the global scope of millions of objects in multiple buckets and Regions. IAM Access Analyzer for S3 only finds buckets exposed to external principals, and Multi-Region Access Points route requests rather than audit versioning configuration.
869: A is correct because an Amazon SQS FIFO queue guarantees that each order is delivered and processed exactly once and in the exact order it was received, which satisfies the exactly-once processing requirement. The queue also buffers orders during unpredictable traffic surges so the application is not overwhelmed, and a Lambda target scales automatically to process the queued orders. An SNS standard topic provides at-least-once delivery without ordering or exactly-once guarantees, AppFlow is for SaaS data transfer, and X-Ray is only a tracing tool.
870: C is correct because creating an IAM role in the Production account with a trust policy that specifies the Development account is the standard cross-account access pattern, allowing the two senior developers to assume the role and gain only the permissions granted to it. This approach avoids creating IAM users or credentials in the Production account and makes it easy to extend access in the beta phase by simply allowing additional developers to assume the same role. The role must live in the account being accessed, so a role in the Development account cannot grant access to Production, and IAM groups cannot be used as cross-account principals.
871: A is correct because Amazon Cognito is a managed, serverless authentication service that scales automatically with user growth and requires no infrastructure to maintain. Lambda@Edge runs authorization logic at CloudFront edge locations close to end users, delivering low login latency, while CloudFront itself serves the web application globally. The AWS Directory Service options require managing a full managed Active Directory, and S3 Transfer Acceleration or Elastic Beanstalk do not provide global edge-based content delivery for the application.
872: D is correct because a service control policy in AWS Organizations enforces the deny rule at the organization level across all member accounts, preventing any user, even administrators, from launching large EC2 instance types. This is a single centralized policy with the least operational overhead compared to managing IAM policies, roles, or permissions for every user in every account. AWS Resource Access Manager is for sharing resources across accounts, not for restricting instance sizes, and per-account IAM changes would need to be repeated repeatedly as accounts and users change.
873: B is correct because AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates OS inventory and patch deployment across hundreds of heterogeneous Windows and Linux EC2 instances from a single managed service. Amazon Inspector performs automated vulnerability scans on the instances and produces scheduled monthly reports summarizing common vulnerabilities and exposures for regular review. Security Hub aggregates security findings rather than scanning for OS vulnerabilities, and Shield, GuardDuty, and AWS Config do not automate operating system patching.
874: A is correct because pre-provisioning the Auto Scaling group and ELB in the DR Region alongside a DynamoDB global table, which asynchronously replicates data across Regions, means the DR environment is always running and DNS failover can shift traffic almost immediately for minimal downtime. CloudFormation-based solutions that launch resources only when a disaster occurs add significant provisioning time during a failover event. The CloudWatch alarm and Lambda option adds unnecessary custom automation when Route 53 DNS failover can handle rerouting directly.
875: D is correct because an S3 gateway endpoint is a free VPC endpoint that routes traffic between the private subnet instances and S3 entirely over the AWS private network, ensuring data never travels across the public internet. It requires only a route table entry and has no hourly or per-GB endpoint charges, making it the most cost-effective compliant option. A NAT gateway would send traffic over the public internet and incurs hourly and data processing charges, Storage Gateway is for hybrid on-premises storage, and an S3 interface endpoint bills an hourly fee per Availability Zone.
876: B is correct because the application is accessible at the transport layer (Layer 4) of the OSI model, and a Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4, distributing TCP traffic across the instances with high availability. D is correct because placing the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones with application health checks automatically replaces unhealthy instances and adds capacity, which eliminates the single-Availability-Zone single point of failure. Combining these two changes distributes traffic across healthy instances in multiple AZs in a cost-effective manner, whereas the other options either address only failover of stopped instances or add unnecessary load balancers.
877: B is correct because Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda is a fully serverless combination that hosts the dynamic contact form logic with zero idle cost, which is ideal for a site with fewer than 100 visits per month since you only pay per request. The second Lambda function publishing to an Amazon SNS topic provides simple email notification to the company when the form is submitted. The ECS, Amplify with server-side scripting, and EC2 with IIS options all involve running and paying for infrastructure that is massively oversized for such low traffic.
878: D is correct because routing the root user email to a centralized company-controlled mailbox through email aliases ensures the root user identity is never tied to a single individual and cannot be lost or left unmonitored when personnel change, which is the most secure practice. Configuring alternate contacts with separate business-managed distribution lists for billing, operations, and security ensures each notification category is delivered to the appropriate team across all accounts. This centralizes control of sensitive root account communications while reliably routing operational, billing, and security notifications to the correct recipients.
879: A is correct because Amazon RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections to the Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, preventing connection exhaustion and timeouts during peak usage while the Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances retries purchases until processing completes. C is correct because sending purchase requests to an Amazon SQS queue decouples the processing tier so surges are buffered in the queue instead of hitting the database all at once, and an Auto Scaling group of instances reading from the queue scales out to drain the backlog cost-effectively. Together these changes let the application absorb unpredictable peak demand without over-provisioning, whereas ElastiCache only helps reads and API Gateway usage plans do not address database saturation.
880: B is correct because Amazon QuickSight is AWS's managed business intelligence service that can publish a custom dashboard with the requested NAT gateway cost table visual and share it with senior leadership across accounts. Amazon Athena can query the AWS Cost and Usage Report files directly in the S3 bucket using standard SQL, and QuickSight uses Athena as its data source, enabling the daily NAT gateway cost breakdown from the beginning of the current month. CloudWatch is a monitoring service that cannot query CUR data, and AWS DataSync is a data transfer tool rather than a query engine.
